# Chapter Nine: Missionaries

His eyes opened to light and white fabric as he tried to understand where he was. “He is awake” came a voice to his left and he looked, the woman walked over to him smiling. “Didn’t think you were going to make it” she gently said, checking his bandages as he lay there, unsure as to where he was, last he remembered were the strange creatures flying from branch to branch through the trees, he had believed demons had come to retrieve him. He looked around him and see the lines of beds with people in various stages of healing or dying. “Where am I” he croaked realizing his throat was completely dry. Try as he might he couldn’t build enough saliva to wet his pallete. The middle-aged woman brought over a small wooden cup and helped him drink, the water soothed his throat and he swallowed greedily. “Not so fast, you have been out for three days Messenger” she said.

“To answer your question, you are at camp hope, we are somewhere just over the border of the Territories, most of those coming from the south end up here” she said, and her eyes fell. “The Sylvan’s are a private people, so here we are until they decide what to do with us” she continued but he could hear the nervous edge to her voice. Nero got it now, they were in a camp, a place for those with no home, those here had fled the south, fled the tyranny of the Empress only to be herded into a place with others like them, not knowing if they would be sent back or allowed to stay. He wondered about the name, camp hope, looking around hope was the one thing this place was devoid of.

Nero sat up, wincing as he did so “Please, rest” she said putting her hands gently on his chest, but Nero resisted. “Madam, I am a servant of Aurtus, I can imagine I am in the one place where he is needed” he finished, getting up from the bed and for a moment the floor swam as he stood up and the nurse came quickly to his aid, steadying him until he could stand on his own. Another woman entered the room stopping at the door she crossed her arms and shot the two of them a disapproving look. “Where do you think you are going sir” she asked, and the tone told Nero she was not happy. “I am needed here maam, I am going to do my job” he said, straightening his back and showing his resolve. “That’s fine Messenger, we could use some hope and faith here, but first I am going to check you over, and there is no arguing that” she said coming over to him.

Nero winced as the woman poked and prodded at his bandages, once in a while offering a disapproving grunt as she continued to check him over. Finally, the doctor rose nodding down to him “You can go Messenger, but I expect you back here tomorrow so that I may check those bandages, do not make me come looking for you” she said pointing a finger at him.

Nero put on his best ‘innocent man of god’ look and nodded to her helping him to his feet they two women stood there as Nero motioned them back, shuffling he hid the winces from pain as it shot up his leg, he had been hurt badly but just seeing this room told him what he needed to know. Nero had been brought here, that even in this dark time Aurtus had not forsaken or forgotten them. He stepped out of the small building and squinted as his eyes adjusted to the bright sun of the mid-day.

He surveyed the camp hope was the name she had told him he thought bitterly as he watched a mother and child dirty and hungry as they crouched by an old tent, not even worthy of being called a shelter. As he continued to look, he saw many families, children and even single adults wandering around still in shock. The place was a mess he noticed as he walked down a row, his tattered messenger robes still draped over his body.

His heart grew heavy the more he walked, the Empress and her mages had destroyed so much in the name of power he thought, offering whispered blessings and prayers to those he passed.

He came to a small rough treelog laid out as a bench and sat down, tired from the exertion of walking and still healing from his wounds Nero closed his eyes My Lord Aurtus, I know you have certainly brought me here for a reason, but forgive me I am weak and my heart is full of hate, surely you show me those who need help and all I see is the destruction wrought on all He thought. 
I will try to help as is my oath Aurtus he finished, the mental prayer making him feel a little better.

A bowl of some kind of gruel floated into his sight and his head came up to find a young man smiling down on him. “Please messenger, eat, you need to keep up your strength” the man said gently. He had a young face but the beard with light lines of grey spoke to experience he thought looking up and studying the man, his eyes were gentle that he could tell, and Nero took the food and motioned for the man to sit next to him. He looked back over the line of people still without food and Nero smiled up at him. I have chosen right he thought.

“Do not worry my child, we will deal with them in a moment” he said to the man. “Messenger, my name is Buris Gilread, this is my partner meric” he said distracted motioning to the small unassuming man next to him, the man’s smile was genuine but Nero could see the worry and concern on the man’s face “I am merely here to ensure my love does not kill himself while trying to play hero” Meric said bowing slightly to the Messenger Nero could make out the worry on both men’s faces, Meric for his partner and Gildread for the people of the camp, this man had taken it upon himself to take care of these people, Nero would need that he thought smiling and putting a hand on his arm. “Meric, I will ensure Gilread comes home to you in one piece, but I will need his help, with your consent of course” Nero asked humbly slightly bowing and Meric’s smile widened “Of course Messenger, wild horses couldn’t keep Buris from helping, but I appreciate your vow and I will hold you to it” Meric finished and giving a light peck on the check to Gilread he turned and left the two men to business, Gilread looked after him and then turned his soulful brown eyes to Nero, searching those of the Messengers. He must have found what he was looking for because he sat down and turned towards the Messenger.

“How did you come to be here Messenger” Gilread asked, Nero smiled knowing the man must have asked that question a million times.

“That’s not important Gilread, who is in charge here?” Nero asked, deciding to get to the point for brevity’s sake, there were still people who needed food and shelter. Gilread’s face fell “I don’t know, in fact I can’t find anyone who is actually running the camp, it more appears they set it up and herd us in. Some supplies show up as the Silvan’s bring them and then leave. The man said, his eyes locking with Nero’s, the man was lost, just going through the motions to try and take care of those who needed it. Nero understood this and simply patted the man’s hand. “Do not worry, Aurtus has sent me here, and you to me my friend. Now we need to get to work”. Getting up he quickly found the pot of gruel and rolling up his sleeves he began to feed those along the row.

They did this for hours, finally he had been able to sit, to rest his body still healing had felt pain for the last few hours, but he overcame it, adding to the penance he felt he owed for the anger in his heart towards the mages and the Empress. Once he had a few moments to rest, Nero was up and walking he needed to organize this place, he needed to ensure that his people were taken care of because make no mistake he thought to himself, these were his people. He approached the small building, the only one that currently existed on the premesis. The hospital took up over two thirds of the structure, but the rest looked as if the doctors and nurses were using it for storage, he could understand that since there was no where else that they could even remotely guarantee cleanliness or sterility he surmised approaching the doctor who stood on the small dilapidated porch. “I need to use the building for a while, I promise not to disturb your supplies” he stated, no introduction no greeting, simply the request. The man looked surprised for a moment and then noticed the robes “Of Course Messenger” he said stepping out of the way of the door. Nero was not blind to the trust and deference the robe brought from most people and smiled.

Gilread joined him soon after. “We need to move these people to either a better location or somewhere we have supplies to build” he stated and Gilread nodded. “For that you will need to talk to the Silvan’s, they are not amenable to our requests so far he said and winced. Nero nodded he was sure that whomever he was dealing with had been more then rude. He had heard the stories about the way they looked about their intolerance for ‘lowlanders’ but he needed to take care of his people and he knew there would be more coming.

“I will take care of it, how are the supplies?” he asked and for the next hour the two of them talked about supplies and logistics to ensure that the people who came were taken care of.

As the sun began to set over the trees and only a few scant hours from Nero even becoming conscious he stood at the gate, waiting patiently. His patience was rewarded sometime later when a man, well not a man like he knew it came out of the forest and stood on the other side of the gate. Nero took notice of the green hue of the creature’s skin and the overly large eyes and narrow face. “I need to speak to someone in charge” he stated officially and waited. The creature, no man he thought, this is a man he said to himself reinforcing it, he couldn’t think of them as creatures or demons, they might look different, but they were men. He nodded to himself as the soldier stood there, finally he turned and shouted something in a language that Nero did not understand and had never heard the like before. It was almost musical he thought but didn’t have time to dwell on it as another soldier emerged from the woods.

The soldier approached the fence, looking the Messenger over “What is the problem” he asked, and Nero sighed a breath of relief, he had been afraid the soldiers wouldn’t be able to understand him.

“The conditions in the camp are deplorable, we need to either move or we need supplies to build out structures to ensure these people are sheltered and taken care of, now whom do I speak to” he said and waited as the soldiers eyes slightly widened, he was not used to be talked to this way Nero thought with a hint of satisfaction. “You have the camp, be happy with that” the soldiers stated and turned to go. “I don’t think so, either you accede to my reasonable requests or I will organize these people and we will go find our own place to stay, how far is your closest city?” Nero asked and the man winced. I win he thought seeing the slight fear in his eyes, though the soldier hid it well. Nero understood the type of orders they would have given this soldier, something like keep them penned, and keep them quiet, but don’t hurt them. Typical buericratic drivel since they didn’t know what to do with the mass of refugees that had began to stream over the border.

The soldier sighed and finally nodded “I will do what I can, I can promise nothing” he stared and then pointed a much too long finger at Nero. “Keep your people here, do not let them wander” he ordered, and Nero nodded bowing slightly to the man.

The next day as nero awoke he heard someone rustling around outside. “Who is there?” he called trying to wipe the sleep out of his eyes and the crick from the cold ground in his back. The tent, again not even an accurate description he thought eyeing the holes in the fabric with an annoyed expression. “Messenger, you have to come see” came the excited voice of Gilread. After a few minutes Nero had extracted himself from the small tent, he reached for the Messenger robe and found it there on the line he had left it on, but it had been repaired and cleaned. He cocked his head and eyed Gilread he shrugged, and a sheepish smile spread across his face. “A few of the women took it upon themselves to repair and clean it” he simply said. Nero nodded and with a smile put the robe on the repaired garment feeling like armor against the pain and malaise that seemed to hang over the camp. Meric approached with two steaming plates of eggs, handing one to Gilread he eyed his parter reproachfully “You forgot to eat love” he simply said and handed the other plate to Nero, taking it he bowed smiling at the interaction between the two, they were in love and there was never a more hopeful sight then that he thought gently taking the fork and eating for a few minutes, once he was done Meric took the plate and waited until Gilread had finished, taking his as well “I am not nearly as adept as Buric in organizing such things, but at the very least I can ensure the two of you don’t fall over from hunger” Meric quipped turning and leaving with the now empty plates.

Gilread’s eyes followed him smiling “Don’t let his humble nature fool you Messenger, I am absolutely sure it was he who organized the women and then ensured they had the equipment they needed to do the repairs, but he would never admit to it, one of the reasons I love that man” Gilread stated and then turned back to focus on the Messenger.

They walked to the entrance of the row to find a stack of planed wood and fresh cloth, in a few boxes he found iron nails, wood pegs and tools left for them. Nero nodded approvingly and got to work organizing the men into groups and as the day progressed small shacks began to populate in rows along the fence of the camp.

By the time the week was out, the entire camp had been transformed, it looked almost like a small city, the men had even built a new keep, though it was wood and cloth that Nero had held his first gathering, thanking Aurtus for his gifts. After the mass he watched the people as they dispersed to head back to the small shacks, and he could see the smiles and hope returning to those who until recently had been without them.

It was a short time later as Nero was reviewing the supplies and food deliveries when Gilread burst through the door of the small shack that doubled as the church starting the Messenger. “What is it?” Nero barked and then taking a breath when he realized the annoyance and fear had leaked out through the statement. “I apologize Gilread, you startled me” he said placing a gentle smile on his face, though one he didn’t feel after reading the deliver reports, food was short and so where most of the other needed supplies, he would have to talk to the Silvan’s about it he mused. “Messenger, we have a problem” Gilread began pulling Nero from his thoughts as he focused on the man, now noticing that his clothing was torn and dirty, it looked as if he had been in a fight thought Nero. “What is it?” He asked leaning forward to reguard his friend and now assistant.

Gilread caught his breath, pulling his fingers through the long dark hair to straighten it, he pulled himself up to his full five-foot ten-inch frame and reguarded the Messenger. “A new batch of refugees came in last night” he began, and Nero looked down to see the written list of those who had entered the camp. “A small group of them have turned out to be thugs, they are taking food and supplies and charging people to live in the shacks, they have taken up residence at the far end and have anointed themselves the leaders” he finished and then looked down at himself. “When I went over to discuss this with them, I was set upon Messenger, what do we do?” His last words were a plea Gildread did not know how to proceed and now looked to the Messenger for guidance.

Nero lowered his head, closing his eyes he calmed himself, hadn’t they gone through enough, hadn’t people who thought themselves better decided to destroy the peace in a pursuit of power and yet here again more people trying to do the same only on a smaller scale, was this so inherint in our makeup that we cannot escape the need to police our own Nero wondered and then opened his eyes locking his gaze on Gilread his eyes steeled with resolve “Go find as many able bodied men as you can, meet back here in one hour” he said dismissing the young man. Nero continued to sit there he was responsible for these people, to help them, aid them and ultimately protect them. It was the duty of his office; his life and he would not shirk that duty he thought standing and walking to the door.

On the hour Nero stood on the small porch of the little shack he used as his church and waited as ten strong men gathered in front of him, he could feel the nervous energy emenating from the small crowd, they had all heard of the new group, of the so called self proclaimed leaders and some had even been victim to them he noticed, as he roved over the gathering he could see anger and fear in every man’s eyes.

Taking a breath Nero steeled his resolve he was a man of peace, a man of comfort but in these trying times in order to lead the flock, one must protect it he thought as he pushed the fear back not allowing it to show on his face as he stood before the men. “Today we find outselves in a position I had hoped we had left behind, those who coveted power beyond all else have enslaved us and driven us from our homes and families” he began turning to pace the small porch as all eyes focused on him. “Unfortunately there are those who have not learned the lessons taught to us by the Black Empress and her mage cronies, so it falls to us to ensure those who feel they can weild power over the weak are shown the proper path, Aurtus’s path” he continued, not knowing where the words came from but they flowed from his lips and he could see the backs straighten on those who had been beaten and held down, told they were nothing better then mundanes, that they only existed to serve there betters.

It is time Nero thought that we take back our destiny, our country and our pride it was at that moment that the hate was given a vehicle one that would drive him the rest of his days, it was left to him to ensure that his people were not taken advantage of or mistreated he thought, his finger within the folders of the robe, in a pocket where a simply gold ring sat. Pulling the ring out he studied it, the sun glinting the crystal centerpiece, slowly he slid the ring upon his finger saying the words, the oath that gave him the power as the voice of Aurtus on this earth. “We will take back our pride, we will keep those safe who cannot save themselves, this is no longer left to the soldiers or the wardens or even the mages, they have all failed us, now it is up to us to ensure our own protection, to forge our own destiny” he said and they stood taller, all the men in front of him. His words resounding within them.

Nero pulled a bucket from behind him where slivers of wood sat innocently and each man grabbed one, holding them as a club as they stood, the new soldiers of Aurtus Nero thought smiling with pride. Nero was no longer simply a messenger but now stood as the Lord Reagent for Vicor, the man responsible for the people and the Messengers who spread the word of the Emissary, he would no longer leave the protection or rule of his people to others. It was time the church took its responsibility and rose above the place it had aloud itself to hold. He would no longer allow those unworthy to rule over his flock he thought looking over his men, his soldiers.

The group of men led by Nero walked the small aisles in between the shacks, he could see the looks from those they passed, eyeing the Messenger and his band of men, hope shone in the eyes of most as they understood what was about to happen, Mothers grabbed there children disappearing into the hovels as others walked behind the group, giving them a bit of distance as they approached the far end of the camp.

Nero looked to see a a small group of large men standing at the end of a row. One of them held a woman by the hair as the largest one laughed at the two. He had one of those looks, the kind that said thug, his bald head shined in the sunlight as he stood there akimbo, ver alpha dog thought Nero wryly. The man had not wanted for much from the look of him he was well overweight but in a way that said he could take care of himself; his crew was smaller but not by much. Nero approached smiling as he did so. “Well met my friends” he said walking up to the group and standing in front of the leader.

The man looking down on the Messenger and leering at him. “Well, well looks like we have a Messenger of Aurtus, here to save us lowly creatures” he said expanding his arms to encompass the group a low chuckle rolled through the others as they stepped forward to stand behind the leader, the one man pushing the crying girl to the ground as he did, something more fun seeming to show up Nero supposed.

The stood there appraising the Messenger and his group of men, all of which had various sticks in their hands, but he did not seem bothered by this fact. Looking to his men a chuckle escaped his lips. “Well now, what are we here to do Messenger, are you here to save us, or perhaps have you come to challenge me for leadership of this place, because I have to tell you, I kind of like it here and don’t plan on stepping down” he said, his eyes wandering to the crying girl on the ground as a lascivious grin spead across his scarred face. “I definitely am going to like it here” he whispered, and Nero tamped down on the revulsion and anger burning hot coals in his stomach as he kept the smile on his face, though now very much forced.

Nero crossed his hands behind his back and looked the other man over, noticing the worn leather armor he wore and the knife with a familiar crest, in fact one was surprised to see in this place, then he placed it. “You are turen protectorate soldiers?” he asked but already knew the answer. The man’s smile fell, and his eyes sharpened as he studied Nero with fresh eyes. “What would you know about that?” he asked suspiciously, and Nero shrugged, I have met a few though I am wondering what soldiers from a forgien land are doing here instead of at home preparing to defend your borders?” he asked causually and could see the anger welling up in the big man. Nero took an involuntary step back he wasn’t sure how to proceed, until that moment he had expected farmers, bullies looking to take advantage of those who were weaker then they were, but instead here were trained and armed soldiers, though only with daggers but still his men may outnumber the soldiers by a few bodies, but they would easily be taken if these men were even half as decent as Nero had heard the trained protectorate were.

The man sighed shaking his head “There is nothing to defend, the Black Empress has mages and well other things, we were part of an expeditionary force sent to retrieve something that had fallen from the sky, except it wasn’t a something, it was a someone and turns out the Empress was looking for em too.” He began and his eyes grew distant as he recalled the events that had led him here. “A Lord Seer and a small group of soldiers showed up we more then outnumbered them and went quickly to the sword, but the seer had these things, two of them white as ghosts and moved like animals but looked almost human, they descended on us, with the power of mages the seer and the two demons tore apart my men, myself and a few others were lucky to be alive, we ran before they could get to us, myself and the few others here Messenger, those creatures chased us for almost two days before we lost them. Whats the point of defending our home against things like that” he finished, and Nero could see the fear, shame and bitterness on the man’s face.

Nero stood back and looked at the group of men. “So why come here and then terrorize those who already have nothing soldiers, why bring misery to a place that already has its lions share” he asked almost pleading, if he could reach the soldier maybe he could convince him to stand down, to help these people but his hopes were dashed quickly as the man’s face transformed into a vicious smile. “Oh Messenger, here we can be kings and I plan on spending my last days before the Empress and her ilk descend on us, living it up, right boys” he called back to his men and they cheered. But his smile quickly vanished as he leaned forward eyeing the Messenger “Now, you and your pitiful bunch of enforcers begone, if I see you again, I will kill you” he said and pushed a finger into the Messengers chest hard enough to make Nero wince.

Standing there caught in indecision Nero did not know what to do, he was no soldier, he had no idea how to lead these men against trained troops and in doubt he took a step back. As he did the large man’s mouth widened into a grin just as a large rock slammed into it causing him to reel. The group of soldiers moved around their leader, knives emerging as they looked around for the threat.

“Did you think you could just move in here; take whatever girls you wanted and do what you wanted and there would be no repurcusions” came a female voice from behind them all. The entire group of men turned to find thirty women standing behind the group, arms crossed as they waited, ready with makeshift weapons. “Did you think we were going to simply allow you to take over, or you to fight without even considering adding our numbers to your little force, of course you didn’t because your men” she said, the last word coming out as if it were an unpleasant smell. The woman was middle age and her thin curvy shape just starting to show a hint of weight to it. But her blonde hair and crystal blue eyes told of a beautiful woman in her prime but there was a hardness too, someone who had seen pain and worked hard to make a life for herself, she did not look like she was one to allow others to easily take the lead.

“So, here is what we are going to do” she began pushing her way through the surprised men and into the center, coming to stand between Nero and the large soldier who was just not recovering from the stone. The man took an aggressive step towards her, but something in her eyes made him pause as the shorter and lighter female stared down the soldier.

“We all have to live here together, so unless you want you and your men to be found with there throats cut, you will do as I say, this camp is now under my leadership, Messenger Nero you have done a wonderful job and will continue to work with me however, we will no longer allow you men to dictate what goes on in the camp, we have all lost our lives, our families and what little dignity we have, we are not about to allow ourselves to become merely pawns in mens powergames” the woman concluded and the two men looked on speechless.

The silene continued to grow as they stood there, the large soldier finally shaking his head. “Who are you” he asked assounted at her brazen nature.

The woman smiled pushing a lock of blonde hair out of her face. “I am vira merchan and I am now the leader of this camp” she said a smile breaking out on her face. The soldiers squared his shoulders and took an aggressive step towards her, but Vira did not move, eyeing the soldier with contempt. “Whats to stop me from killing both of you and simply declaring myself leader” he said a small smile reappearing, despite the fat lip and blood that was smeared over his cheek.

Vira returned the smile shaking her head “Because while you men were searching for sticks to smack youself with so you could show each other how strong and fierce you are, we went and simply asked the soldiers for these.” She finished waving her hand back to a line of woman who until now had gone unnoticed. At that moment all six of them brandished rifles and pistols, leveling them at the group of men, who quickly took a step back as doubt and fear spread over there face.

The big man was no fool and knew when he was beaten, dropping his knife he raised his arms “This is not over woman, I will kill you” he said and within a moment a blue blaze of energy snapped his head back and his body crumpled to the ground. “Like I am going to let you live to try that” she laughed turning to the Messenger who stood their mouth agape. “You killed an unarmed man” he said meeting her eyes, she smiled gently and nodded “Yes, I did because had I not he would have found a way to take over and kill us” she said pragmatically.

“Now Messenger, we have work do to, do you think you can follow a woman?” she asked, and the entire crowd was silent as he stood there reguarding her finally he simply nodded, and a collective sigh went over the crowd. “I acceeed to your authority Vira, what now?” he simply said, Nero knew he now led the church, but he no longer led the camp, this woman had organized the woman and shown her ability to lead this group.

Cocking her head Vira reguarded the Messenger “No messenger, you have done a very good job at organizing and leading us, you just have no experience when it comes to ensuring the safety of those you watch over, so that you will leave to me and I shall assist as I can. I have no interest in taking over, just making sure that we all have a voice in this place” she finished, and a cheer erupted from the women behind them. The men eyeing the line of gun toting women behind them.

With a nod the two headed back towards the Messengers tent, the armed women accompanying them along with Gilread, everyone else merely broke up the men who had followed the large soldier simply ignored now as they stood there gawking at the outcome.

Nero leaned into his compatriot and friend “So, why is it you two aren’t married?” he asked keeping his voice low and watched as Gilread blushed. “Never the right time, Meric keeps asking me and I keep putting him off, I love him Messenger, I want that moment to be perfect and I can never seem to find the right moment when it will be” he finished and shrugged, his normally capable demeanor overshadowed by the sheer boyish nature of the shrug. Nero walked for a moment thinking and then turned back to the man “We have a finite amount of time in this earth Gilread, take what you have for as long as you have it, if you love him, give Meric the honor of making him your mate” he finished and then continued on, letting the conversation fall at that. There was no point in beating the poor man over the head with it he thought.

Nero sped up leaving Gilread behind and caught up to Vira just as the two made it back to the tent the woman turned and spoke to her armed compatriots who dispursed and walked there separate ways with a purpose as she turned back to Nero “We now have police, these women are no strangers to weapons or to war, but most men simply disreguard us as property, now we plan on changing that Messenger and this is where we do that” she said smiling and Nero smiled back nodding. “Of course, Vira” he said and was about to continue when he noticed one of the Silvan’s had entered the camp, standing back and eyeing the lowlanders nervously as he waited to speak. Turning to him he nodded at the Soldier “What can we do for you?” he asked and the soldier approached his mastery of the language was rudimentary but understandable “Soldiers will come soon, we prepare for war, you defend camp” he simply said and turned walking way, leaving the Messenger and Vira stunned as they watched him leave.

“Looks like we have preparations to make Vira” he said and the woman, her face solem as she nodded to him. “Together Messenger, together”
